claim: Whether a built thing is recognised depends more on the viewpoint than on its content, and survives losing a cue only if it has several: the locomotive was named from 5 of 7 angles and survived losing any one of wheels, smoke, face or chimney; the carriage was never a train from the platform (only its livery said so) and was one from the track where rails, skirt and an end were in view. A view must be filled by the thing, or the room gets named.
evidence: tools.critic_lab, knowledge/blood/critic-bench/lab-1, one change at a time, ~90 single-picture questions to Sol (2026-11-19). Renderer brightness 0 vs 8 changed nothing.
use: Give a thing several independent cues and make sure they are in view from where the player meets it; ask a critic for the one change that would make the view read, which gave usable, repeated advice.
